This conversation uses two-stage tool calling. First, call exactly the meta-tool below; do not call a real tool before the tool response arrives. Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Then call that real tool exactly once for the original user request, using its exact function name and parameter keys. Your second assistant turn must have exactly this complete form, not a bare arguments object: <tool_call>
{"name":"<selected real name>","arguments":{...}}
</tool_call>. Do not repeat the meta-tool after the tool response and do not emit prose.

Meta-tool schema:
{
  "type": "function",
  "function": {
    "name": "select_tool",
    "description": "Choose the one real tool that should handle the query.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "tool_name": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": [
            "nectar_tool",
            "saffron_tool",
            "syrinx_tool",
            "obsidian_tool",
            "bramble_tool",
            "cobalt_tool",

            "lichen_tool"
          ]
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "tool_name"
      ],
      "additionalProperties": false
    }
  }
}

Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Hi there! I'm Kathy, and I've just launched a new line of Andalusian-Moroccan fusion spice blends on the marketplace. I need help reviewing what customers are asking about them. Could you pull the latest list of product questions or concerns from the platform? I want to make sure my responses reflect both the Southern flavors folks expect and the Mediterranean twist that makes these blends unique. Oh, and if there are any recurring themes in the questions, could you highlight those too? It’d help me tweak my product descriptions or maybe even inspire new recipes.

This conversation uses two-stage tool calling. First, call exactly the meta-tool below; do not call a real tool before the tool response arrives. Return only one JSON call inside <tool_call></tool_call> tags, with tool_name set to one enum value. After that call, you will receive a <tool_response> containing the selected real tool schema. Then call that real tool exactly once for the original user request, using its exact function name and parameter keys. Your second assistant turn must have exactly this complete form, not a bare arguments object: <tool_call>
{"name":"<selected real name>","arguments":{...}}
</tool_call>. Do not repeat the meta-tool after the tool response and do not emit prose.

{
  "type": "function",
  "function": {
    "name": "select_tool",
    "description": "Choose the one real tool that should handle the query.",
    "parameters": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {

          "type": "string",

    }
  }
}

I'm creating a networking event campaign and need to generate personalized placeholder headshots for 30 attendees based on their actual professional backgrounds. I have a list of attendees' names and current companies. Can you help me search for their LinkedIn profiles to understand their roles and industries, then create realistic AI-generated headshots that reflect each person's professional context? For example, I'd start with "Sarah Chen" who works at "NVIDIA" - can you find her LinkedIn info and generate a professional headshot that incorporates elements relevant to her tech/AI background?
